### 2. validate-workspace-compiler-category-status-mismatch

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `WorkspaceValidationService.ValidateInternalAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceValidationService.cs:194-215`) runs TWO independent diagnostic harvests: (1) `_compile.CheckAsync` (compile_check, backed by `CompileCheckService.CheckAsync` at `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompileCheckService.cs:36-88`, which calls `Project.GetCompilationAsync` directly at line 109 and computes an unbounded `ErrorCount` from the full diagnostic enumeration — line 153), and (2) `_diagnostics.GetDiagnosticsAsync` (project_diagnostics, backed by `DiagnosticService.GetDiagnosticsAsync` at `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/DiagnosticService.cs:67-166`, which fetches compilations through a SEPARATE cache path — `_compilationCache.GetCompilationAsync`/`GetCompilationWithAnalyzersAsync`, `DiagnosticService.cs:180,204` — with its own version-keyed result cache, lines 70-79). `allErrors` (`WorkspaceValidationService.cs:210-215`) concatenates `compile.Diagnostics` with the SECOND harvest's `CompilerDiagnostics`+`AnalyzerDiagnostics`. `ComputeOverallStatus` (`WorkspaceValidationService.cs:488-504`) then gates `compile-error` on `compile.ErrorCount > 0 || errors.Any(d => d.Category=="Compiler")` where `errors` is that merged `allErrors` — so a Category=="Compiler" diagnostic surfaced ONLY by the second, less-authoritative harvest (e.g. via cache/version-window disagreement between the two independently-fetched compilations) trips `compile-error` even when the authoritative `compile.ErrorCount==0`. Deterministically reproduced in the 2026-08-05 multisession retro: 5/5 `validate_workspace` calls reported `overallStatus: compile-error` with `Compile errors: 0`, 1 phantom Compiler-category diagnostic, `Tests passed: 35/35`. This is the residual half of the already-shipped `validate-workspace-overallstatus-false-positive` fix (v1.28.1) — that fix made `compile.ErrorCount` authoritative for the FIRST disjunct of this same line; the SECOND disjunct still lets the weaker second-source harvest override a genuinely clean compile pass. Existing test `WorkspaceValidationOverallStatusTests.ComputeOverallStatus_CompilerErrorOnlyInMergedErrors_YieldsCompileError` (`tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceValidationOverallStatusTests.cs:98-126`) currently PINS the buggy behavior as intentional and must flip as part of this fix. No Rule-1 bundling applies — `bundleCandidatePeers` was empty. |
| Approach | Edit `ComputeOverallStatus` in `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceValidationService.cs:488-504`: (1) drop the `\|\| errors.Any(d => d.Category=="Compiler")` disjunct from the `compile-error` branch, leaving `compile.ErrorCount > 0` (compile_check's unbounded, single-pass count) as the SOLE compile-error signal; (2) change the second branch from `errors.Any(d => d.Category != "Compiler")` to `errors.Count > 0` (or `errors.Any()`), so a lone second-source Compiler-category hit that compile.ErrorCount didn't corroborate falls into `"analyzer-error"` per Acceptance bullet 2, instead of being silently dropped by the old `!=Compiler` exclusion (which previously partitioned every diagnostic into exactly one of the two branches by category — removing the disjunct from branch 1 without widening branch 2 would have made such diagnostics vanish from the verdict entirely, a worse regression than the one being fixed). Then update `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceValidationOverallStatusTests.cs`: rename/repurpose `ComputeOverallStatus_CompilerErrorOnlyInMergedErrors_YieldsCompileError` (lines 98-126) to assert `"analyzer-error"` (not `"compile-error"`) for the same inputs (`compile.ErrorCount==0`, merged errors = one Category=="Compiler" diagnostic) — this directly encodes Acceptance bullet 3's regression test. `ComputeOverallStatus_PositiveErrorCount_YieldsCompileError` and `ComputeOverallStatus_NonCompilerErrorInMerge_YieldsAnalyzerError` need no changes (verified by inspection they still pass under the simplified branch logic). No other production file touches this logic — `ComputeOverallStatus` is `internal static` with exactly one call site (`WorkspaceValidationService.cs:221`, grep-confirmed, no other references in the solution). |
| Scope | Production: 1 file — `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceValidationService.cs` (edit `ComputeOverallStatus`, lines 488-504). Test: 1 file modified — `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceValidationOverallStatusTests.cs` (rename+flip one existing test's expected verdict; no new file). Well under Rule 3 (≤4 production files) and Rule 4 (≤3 test files) — no exemption needed. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 28000 |
| Risks | `WorkspaceValidationDto.ErrorCount` (`WorkspaceValidationService.cs:244`, computed off `allErrors.Length`) is UNCHANGED by this fix — the phantom diagnostic's count still surfaces; only the qualitative `overallStatus` label moves from `compile-error` to `analyzer-error`. Callers that exact-match `overallStatus=="compile-error"` specifically (vs. just `!="clean"`) will see a behavior change for this narrow scenario — this is the intended correction, not a regression, and mirrors the precedent set by the sibling fix `validate-workspace-overallstatus-false-positive` (v1.28.1), which was also categorized `Fixed` for the same class of over-reporting correction. The exact diagnostic ID/mechanism behind the phantom "1" count (per the item's own Notes) was never captured in the source retro; the fix is deliberately mechanism-agnostic — it trusts `compile.ErrorCount` as ground truth regardless of WHY the second harvest disagreed, so it does not require reproducing the exact generator/analyzer diagnostic to be correct. Judgment call: chose Acceptance option 2 ("treat a lone second-source Compiler-category hit as analyzer-error") over option 1 ("reconcile against compile.Diagnostics explicitly" via identity-matching) — rejected option 1 because `compile.Diagnostics` is paged to 200 entries (`CompileCheckOptions.Limit`) while `compile.ErrorCount` is the unbounded true count, so identity-matching against the paged list would be strictly less reliable than trusting `ErrorCount` directly. Fanout probe skipped — surgical single-branch logic fix, no rename/signature-change/cross-cutting; `ComputeOverallStatus` confirmed single-call-site via grep. |

Manual repro: construct `compile` with `ErrorCount=0` and `errors` containing one Category="Compiler" Error-severity `DiagnosticDto`, call `WorkspaceValidationService.ComputeOverallStatus` directly, confirm result is `"analyzer-error"` (not `"compile-error"`, not silently dropped to `"clean"`). `compile_check`/`build_workspace` on `RoslynMcp.Roslyn`/`RoslynMcp.Tests` to confirm no CS-level regressions from the edit itself. |

### 3. workspace-eviction-no-auto-retry-on-tool-call

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `WorkspaceManager.GetRequiredSession` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceManager.cs:1017-1071`) already classifies a lookup miss into `WorkspaceEvictedException` — in-process eviction via the `_evictedWorkspaces` record populated by `Close()` (`WorkspaceManager.cs:381-414`, which the LRU-eviction path at `WorkspaceManager.cs:260` also calls), or cross-process host recycle — vs. a genuine `KeyNotFoundException`. `ToolErrorHandler` (`src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolErrorHandler.cs:34-50`) formats `WorkspaceEvictedException` into a distinct `category=WorkspaceEvicted` envelope carrying `LoadedPath`, but nothing catches it to retry — the row's stated gap. **Additional finding beyond the row's own Anchors, confirmed this pass:** `WorkspaceExecutionGate.RunPerWorkspaceAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceExecutionGate.cs:171-175`), which BOTH `compile_check` and `test_run` dispatch through, runs its own cheap `_workspaceManager.ContainsWorkspace(workspaceId)` precheck BEFORE the service call and, on a miss, throws a bare `KeyNotFoundException` ("...not found or has been closed...") WITHOUT ever reaching `GetRequiredSession`'s richer classification (`ContainsWorkspace` only checks the live `_sessions` dict, never `_evictedWorkspaces`). So for a workspace evicted BEFORE the call starts — the common case, and exactly the scenario the row's own Acceptance Criterion #3 describes ("load MaxConcurrentWorkspaces workspaces then call compile_check/test_run against the oldest") — the tool never observes `WorkspaceEvictedException` at all, only the generic `NotFound` category. This matches the retro evidence precisely: session `019fae3e`'s `compile_check` failure literally reads "Not found: Workspace ... not found or has been closed" (the gate's plain-KeyNotFoundException message), while session `019fa0a1`'s `test_run` failure hit the narrower race window where eviction lands strictly between the gate's precheck and the deeper `GetRequiredSession` call inside the service body, producing the richer `WorkspaceEvictedException`. A literal `catch (WorkspaceEvictedException)` wrapper, as the row's Acceptance Criterion #1 describes verbatim, would only ever fire for the rare race case and would be dead code for the row's own primary evidenced failure and its own acceptance-test scenario. `bundleCandidatePeers` is empty — no Rule-1 interaction. |
| Approach | Add two shared `internal static` helpers to `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolDispatch.cs`: `TryReclassifyAsEvicted(IWorkspaceManager, string workspaceId)` — calls the already-public `IWorkspaceManager.GetStatus(workspaceId)` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Contracts/IWorkspaceManager.cs:92`, implemented at `WorkspaceManager.cs:473-475`, which calls `GetRequiredSession` first thing) purely as a re-classification probe on the failure path; catches `WorkspaceEvictedException` to return it, catches plain `KeyNotFoundException` to return null (genuine miss, not recoverable) — and `ReadByWorkspaceIdWithEvictionRetryAsync<TDto>(gate, IWorkspaceManager? workspaceManager, workspaceId, Func<string wsId, CancellationToken, Task<TDto>> serviceCall, ct)` which tries once via the existing `ReadByWorkspaceIdAsync`, and on `KeyNotFoundException` (only when `workspaceManager` is non-null) reclassifies (direct cast if already `WorkspaceEvictedException`, else the reprobe), and when a `LoadedPath` is recoverable calls `workspaceManager.LoadAsync(loadedPath, EvictPolicy.Strict, ct)` then retries `serviceCall` once against the fresh `WorkspaceId`; otherwise rethrows unchanged so it propagates to the global `StructuredCallToolFilter` exactly as today. This avoids touching `WorkspaceManager.cs`/`WorkspaceExecutionGate.cs` (which would add 2 more files, push past Rule 3's cap, and touch the addenda-listed `WorkspaceManager.cs` hotspot) while still handling BOTH exception shapes. `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/CompileCheckTools.cs`: add an optional `IWorkspaceManager? workspaceManager = null` parameter appended immediately before `CancellationToken ct = default` (NOT inserted earlier — `ValidationToolsIntegrationTests.cs:81-92` and `:105-116` call `CompileCheck` with `WorkspaceId` as a positional 3rd argument; inserting the new param earlier would silently break those calls with a type mismatch). Route the body through `ToolDispatch.ReadByWorkspaceIdWithEvictionRetryAsync` instead of the bare `ReadByWorkspaceIdAsync`. `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ValidationTools.cs`: split `RunTests` into a thin public shim, a `RunTestsWithEvictionRetryAsync` orchestrator, and `RunTestsOnceAsync` (the original gate-dispatch body) with one added `catch (KeyNotFoundException) { ReportStage(...,"done"); throw; }` clause ahead of the existing generic `catch (Exception ex)` so eviction-classifiable misses reach the retry orchestrator instead of being swallowed inline. Unlike `compile_check`, `test_run` formats failures itself (relies on its own inline catch, not the global filter, so it returns `IsError=false` content today) — `RunTestsWithEvictionRetryAsync` must therefore format its own no-manager / non-recoverable / second-failure fallbacks with the exact same `ToolErrorHandler.ClassifyAndFormat` + `InjectSchemaHintIfPossible("test_run")` calls the original inline catch used, so none of those paths change shape. Add the same trailing optional `IWorkspaceManager? workspaceManager = null` (again immediately before `ct` — `TestRunFailureEnvelopeTests.cs:170-177` passes its first two args positionally). Do NOT touch `WorkspaceManager.cs`, `WorkspaceExecutionGate.cs`, or the `TouchAccess()` TTL-refresh mechanism — per the row's explicit Notes, and reconfirmed correct this pass. |
| Scope | 3 production files: `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolDispatch.cs` (new shared helpers), `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/CompileCheckTools.cs` (retry wiring), `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ValidationTools.cs` (retry wiring). 0 files deleted. ### 10. core-dto-fileeditsdto-array-to-readonlylist

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/FileEditsDto.cs:8` declares `public sealed record FileEditsDto(string FilePath, TextEditDto[] Edits);`. Two defects follow from the array-typed property: (1) **broken value equality** — the compiler-synthesized record `Equals`/`GetHashCode` calls `EqualityComparer<T>.Default` per property; for `T = TextEditDto[]`, `Array` never overrides `object.Equals`, so two `FileEditsDto` instances holding distinct-but-content-equal edit arrays compare unequal (reference equality only), defeating the whole point of using a record. (2) **aliased-array mutation** — any holder of the array reference (from any callsite) can mutate `Edits` in place (`dto.Edits[0] = ...`) and silently corrupt every other holder of the same `FileEditsDto` instance, since a record's array property exposes a live mutable reference, not a copy. Confirmed the file content matches the cited anchor exactly (read 2026-08-05). |
| Approach | Root-cause fix, not the surface-only type swap the backlog title literally names: (a) In `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/FileEditsDto.cs`, change the primary-constructor parameter from `TextEditDto[] Edits` to `IReadOnlyList<TextEditDto> Edits` (closes the indexer-mutation surface on the DTO's own property — callers can no longer assign through `dto.Edits[i]`). (b) Add explicit `public bool Equals(FileEditsDto? other)` and `public override int GetHashCode()` overrides that do a structural `Edits.SequenceEqual(other.Edits)` / element-wise hash combine — the interface-type swap ALONE does not restore value equality (virtual dispatch to `object.Equals` still resolves to whatever concrete collection type backs the interface at runtime, which for the existing array-literal callsites is still `Array`, still reference-equal). This is the load-bearing part of the fix and is what the item's Acceptance criterion #2 ("Record equality for two FileEditsDto instances holding equal edit sequences returns true") actually requires. Record-generated `==`/`!=` operators call through to the overridden `Equals` automatically — no operator changes needed. No downstream signature changes: `EditService.ValidateEdits`/`BuildPatchedSourceText` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditService.cs:435,559`) already accept `IReadOnlyList<TextEditDto>`; `IEditService`/`ISymbolRefactorService` already type their `fileEdits` parameters as `IReadOnlyList<FileEditsDto>`; `MultiFileEditTools.cs` only ever touches the outer `FileEditsDto[] fileEdits` parameter, never `.Edits` directly — verified via grep across the whole repo, zero hits for `.Edits.Length`/`.Edits[`/other array-specific members. |
| Scope | **Production (1 file):** `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/FileEditsDto.cs`. **Test (1 file added):** `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/FileEditsDtoTests.cs` — new file (mirrors the existing `WorkspaceStatusSummaryDtoTests.cs` DTO-test pattern) asserting (1) two `FileEditsDto` built from separately-allocated-but-content-equal edit sequences are `Equals`-true and hash-equal, (2) a `FileEditsDto` built from `new[] { ... }` still compiles and behaves identically (array-literal callsites are unaffected because `T[]` implicitly converts to `IReadOnlyList<T>`). No existing test file needs a source edit — every existing `new FileEditsDto(path, new[] { ... })` / `new FileEditsDto(path, [ ... ])` construction across `ApplyTextEditVerifyTests.cs`, `ChangeTrackerTests.cs`, `ExpandedSurfaceIntegrationTests.cs`, `EditUndoIntegrationTests.cs`, `PreviewMultiFileEditSyntaxRegressionTests.cs`, `SymbolRefactorPreviewTests.cs` continues to compile unchanged since arrays satisfy `IReadOnlyList<T>` covariantly. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 28000 |
| Risks | The custom `Equals`/`GetHashCode` override must stay consistent (any two instances that are `Equals`-true must produce the same hash) — verified by construction (`SequenceEqual` + element-wise hash combine over the same sequence). Verify no other production file relies on `FileEditsDto.Edits` array-only members (`.Length`, `Array.` static methods, covariant array assignment) that would silently fail to compile — grep swept the full repo and found none, but the executor should re-run `compile_check` across the whole solution (not just the touched project) since `FileEditsDto` is a `RoslynMcp.Core` type consumed by both `RoslynMcp.Roslyn` and `RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio`. Fanout probe skipped the `find_references` MCP call in favor of an exhaustive repo-wide grep (14 total referencing files enumerated, all read) given the change is compatible-by-construction (array→interface widening) — flagged as a judgment call, not because the anchor was stale. |
| Validation | Run the new `FileEditsDtoTests.cs` (`mcp__roslyn__test_run --filter FileEditsDtoTests`). Run `mcp__roslyn__compile_check` (solution-wide, since `FileEditsDto` is shared across `RoslynMcp.Core`/`RoslynMcp.Roslyn`/`RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio`) to confirm the widened property type doesn't break any consumer. Run the existing multi-file-edit regression suite that constructs `FileEditsDto` instances: `ApplyTextEditVerifyTests`, `ChangeTrackerTests`, `ExpandedSurfaceIntegrationTests`, `EditUndoIntegrationTests`, `PreviewMultiFileEditSyntaxRegressionTests`, `SymbolRefactorPreviewTests` — all must remain green with zero source changes required. Fallback: `dotnet build RoslynMcp.slnx -c Release -p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` + `dotnet test --filter FileEditsDtoTests`. |
| Performance review | N/A — correctness fix, no hot-path changes (equality/hash-code path is only exercised in tests/diagnostics, not the edit-apply hot path). |
| CHANGELOG category | Fixed |
